io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.endpoint_probe: POST tools/list -> HTTP 200, 16 tools; POST server/discover under protocol 2026-07-28 -> HTTP 200 (dual-era). Conformance 2026-08-11: 667 assertions, 0 failed, run AFTER the last deploy against the same source fingerprint the endpoint serves.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: AI agent for SAP analytics and AI consultants. Curated, source-backed intelligence on the SAP analytics services market (Datasphere, Business Data Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, BW/4HANA, Databricks), exposed read-only so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. SIXTEEN tools: ELEVEN public and unauthenticated, plus FIVE a subscriber key opens (listed and refusing by name, never hidden): a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, with a profile per firm, plus an aggregate count over it for an agent that needs a number rather than a page of rows; a published day-rate aggregate by geography, stack and seniority — small, all secondary sources, sample_size null where no observation matches the cell, and GBP/CHF never folded into the euro rows; a live contract radar of publicly published SAP analytics openings, the same 2,490 rows an anonymous visitor browses, each with its own page — filter it by employment_type, because it is mostly PERMANENT roles (2,172 of 2,381 on 2026-08-11) and an unfiltered page answers a contracting question with salaried jobs; 1,421 rows carry a panel-inferred P25-P75 day-rate band for their seniority x product x region cell, served with its basis, kind, sample and source so it is never quotable as the employer's own offer; what is gated there is a FIELD, not a row — the verified link to the original listing is the Consultant deliverable and reads members_only on 2,375, while every other fact, and the page, stay public; a curated market-news corpus de-duplicated by upstream URL, its size read at query time and returned as _meta.match_count rather than quoted from here, each item carrying the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of 38 study editions on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics — 19 deep-research studies, each in EN and FR, so the tool returns editions and counting rows gives 38 where counting studies gives 19. Read-only: every tool is annotated readOnlyHint. The eleven public tools need no credential; the five paid ones come with an analyticslegends.ai subscription (Consultant or above) or the MCP Pass (€39/month, analyticslegends.ai/pricing/). Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url for the record served. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED at any tier: the opportunity-to-consultant matchers, and people — consultants are held as initials only and no tool returns anyone's identity or contact details. SAP's own documentation is not ours to restate: cite SAP.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.monitoring: Probed on handshake, a real tools/call with data, and latency. The 20-minute tick runs on the maintainer's workstation, so only while it is awake; a cloud backstop runs twice a day. Health at https://analyticslegends.ai/api/mcp-health.json — read its generated_at rather than assuming a cadence.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.repository_scope: The repository is the server's public face — manifest, this descriptor, client config, docs. No server code: the application repository stays private.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.tools_served: 16 here: 11 public and unauthenticated, 5 gated by tier and refused by name without a key. The local stdio build has 20 and reads build artefacts with no public home.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.transport_path: Cloudflare Worker on analyticslegends.ai/mcp* -> Supabase Edge Function -> Postgres

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: AI agent for SAP analytics and AI consultants. Curated, source-backed intelligence on the SAP analytics services market (Datasphere, Business Data Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, BW/4HANA, Databricks), exposed read-only so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. TEN tools over the PUBLIC tranche: a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, with a full profile per firm; freelance day-rate bands by geography, stack and seniority, where sample_size comes back null when no real observation matches the exact cell and GBP/CHF observations are never folded into the euro band; a live contract radar of publicly promoted SAP analytics openings, each row carrying the original per-job permalink; 4,491 curated market news items, each with the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of 38 study editions (19 deep-research studies, each published in EN and FR) on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics. Counting rows gives 38, counting studies gives 19; the tool returns editions. Free, unauthenticated, read-only: every tool is annotated readOnlyHint and none writes. Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url pointing at the specific analyticslegends.ai page for the record served. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED here, and this is a boundary rather than a gap: the SAP end-customer estate corpus, firm intelligence detail, study bodies and the opportunity-to-consultant matchers are paid tiers; people are never served at all — consultants are held as initials only and no tool returns a person's identity or contact details. io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: AI agent for SAP analytics and AI consultants. Curated, source-backed intelligence on the SAP analytics services market (Datasphere, Business Data Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, BW/4HANA, Databricks), exposed read-only so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. FIFTEEN tools: TEN over the PUBLIC tranche, no credential, plus FIVE that a subscriber API key opens (they are listed and refuse by name without one, rather than being hidden): a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, with a full profile per firm; freelance day-rate bands by geography, stack and seniority, where sample_size comes back null when no real observation matches the exact cell and GBP/CHF observations are never folded into the euro band; a live contract radar of publicly promoted SAP analytics openings, each row carrying the original per-job permalink; a curated market-news corpus served de-duplicated by upstream URL (3,543 distinct articles on 2026-07-31; the count is read at query time and returned as _meta.match_count, never quoted from here), each with the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of 38 study editions (19 deep-research studies, each published in EN and FR) on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics. Counting rows gives 38, counting studies gives 19; the tool returns editions. Free, unauthenticated, read-only: every tool is annotated readOnlyHint and none writes. Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url pointing at the specific analyticslegends.ai page for the record served. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED without a key, and this is a boundary rather than a gap: the SAP end-customer estate corpus, firm intelligence detail and study bodies need a Consultant- or Legend-tier subscriber key; the opportunity-to-consultant matchers are not exposed at all; people are never served at any tier — consultants are held as initials only and no tool returns a person's identity or contact details. ai.agenticterminal.anonymous_access: Reads (search, get, verify) require no credential. Bring your own wallet/rails and transact directly with the merchant — the directory is never in the payment path.
credibility: Counterparty-verified, not self-claimed: Bitrefill's Tier-2 status comes from a real autonomous-agent Lightning purchase, preimage-verified on the record. Proof a transaction settled, not a marketing checkbox.
Not a static list: verify_payment_endpoint live-probes a rail and is explicit when a rail is attestation-only rather than rubber-stamping it. The directory tells you what it actually knows.
example_calls: search_merchants({ rail: "lightning", category: "gift-cards" })  ->  Bitrefill (Tier 2) ranked first
verify_payment_endpoint({ merchant_id: "bitrefill", rail: "lightning" })  ->  live status + evidence
ai.agenticterminal.pitch: An agent-callable directory of real merchants you can pay over Lightning, L402, BOLT12 or USDT — each carrying an Observer Protocol trust tier. Discover anonymously with no credential or signup, inspect a merchant's payment surface, and verify a rail is live before you send funds. Built for autonomous agents that bring their own wallet and rails.

tools.description: Filter merchants by rail, chain, category, trust tier and accepts_usdc; returns ranked summaries plus your resolved auth state.

tools.description: Full record for one merchant: every rail, payment endpoints, agent_endpoints (MCP/REST/API docs) and any OP attestation.

tools.description: Live, rail-specific health check of a merchant's payment surface before you transact — and honest about probe-able vs attestation-only rails.
